e-3644.knowledge_point: Differentiating Expressions Involving the Cosecant Function
e-3644.worked_solution:
Here, we just take the constant out of the derivative and use the result for the derivative of $\csc x,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(2csc⁡x) \\  & =2\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(csc⁡x) \\  & =2(-csc⁡xcot⁡x) \\  & =-2csc⁡xcot⁡x\end{aligned}
$$

e-3646.knowledge_point: Differentiating Expressions Involving the Cotangent Function
e-3646.problem: Find $\dfrac {\textrm d y} {\textrm d x}$ if $y = 2x - 3\cot x.$
e-3646.worked_solution:
We take the derivative of each term and then add them, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(2x-3cot⁡x) \\  & =2-3(-{csc}^{2}⁡x) \\  & =2+3{csc}^{2}⁡x\end{aligned}
$$

e-3647.knowledge_point: Differentiating Expressions Involving the Secant Function
e-3647.worked_solution:
We use the product rule, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(xsec⁡x) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(x)\cdot sec⁡x+x\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(sec⁡x) \\  & =(1)\cdot sec⁡x+x\cdot (sec⁡xtan⁡x) \\  & =sec⁡x(1+xtan⁡x)\end{aligned}
$$

e-3648.knowledge_point: Finding the Slope of the Tangent at a Point of a Function Involving Reciprocal Trigonometric Functions
e-3648.problem: Find the slope of $y=f(x)$ at $x=\dfrac{\pi}{4}$ if $f(x) = \dfrac{-2\cot x}{\sin x}.$
e-3648.worked_solution:
First, we calculate the derivative using the quotient rule:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{-2cot⁡x}{sin⁡x}) \\  & =\frac{\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(-2cot⁡x)\cdot sin⁡x-(-2cot⁡x)\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(sin⁡x)}{{[sin⁡x]}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{-2(-{csc}^{2}⁡x)\cdot sin⁡x+2cot⁡x\cdot (cos⁡x)}{{sin}^{2}⁡x} \\  & =\frac{2csc⁡x+2cot⁡xcos⁡x}{{sin}^{2}⁡x}\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we substitute $x=\dfrac{\pi}{4}$ in the derivative and get

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{4}) & =\frac{2csc⁡(\frac{\pi }{4})+2cot⁡(\frac{\pi }{4})cos⁡(\frac{\pi }{4})}{{sin}^{2}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4})} \\  & =\frac{2\cdot (\sqrt{2})+2\cdot (1)\cdot (\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2})}{{(\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2})}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{3\sqrt{2}}{(\frac{1}{2})} \\  & =6\sqrt{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 1
?

Find f′(x) if f(x)=2xcsc⁡x.

a
csc⁡x(2xln⁡2+cot⁡x)
b
2xcsc⁡x(ln⁡2+cot⁡x)
c
csc⁡x(2xln⁡2−cot⁡x)
d
2xcsc⁡x(ln⁡2−cot⁡x)
e
2xln⁡2csc⁡xcot⁡x
Submit

decision.explanation: By the product rule, f'(x)=2^x ln(2)csc(x)-2^x csc(x)cot(x)=2^x csc(x)(ln(2)-cot(x)), which matches option d.

after.name: Question 1
after.worked_solution:
We calculate the derivative using the product rule, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({2}^{x}csc⁡x) \\  & ={2}^{x}ln⁡2(csc⁡x)+{2}^{x}(-csc⁡xcot⁡x) \\  & ={2}^{x}csc⁡x(ln⁡2-cot⁡x)\end{aligned}
$$

after.html:
Question 1
?

Find f′(x) if f(x)=2xcsc⁡x.

a
csc⁡x(2xln⁡2+cot⁡x)
b
2xcsc⁡x(ln⁡2+cot⁡x)
c
csc⁡x(2xln⁡2−cot⁡x)
d
2xcsc⁡x(ln⁡2−cot⁡x)
e
2xln⁡2csc⁡xcot⁡x
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

We calculate the derivative using the product rule, as follows:

f′(x)=ddx(2xcsc⁡x)=2xln⁡2(csc⁡x)+2x(−csc⁡xcot⁡x)=2xcsc⁡x(ln⁡2−cot⁡x)

content.knowledge_point: Differentiating Expressions Involving the Cosecant Function
content.worked_solution:
We calculate the derivative using the product rule, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({2}^{x}csc⁡x) \\  & ={2}^{x}ln⁡2(csc⁡x)+{2}^{x}(-csc⁡xcot⁡x) \\  & ={2}^{x}csc⁡x(ln⁡2-cot⁡x)\end{aligned}
$$

Question 2
?

Find f′(x) if f(x)=x2−6csc⁡x.

a
2x2−6csc⁡xcot⁡x
b
−2+6csc⁡xcot⁡x
c
2x+6csc⁡xcot⁡x
d
x+6csc⁡xcot⁡x
e
2+6csc⁡xcot⁡x
Submit

decision.explanation: The derivative of x^2 is 2x, and the derivative of csc(x) is -csc(x)cot(x). Thus f'(x)=2x-6(-csc(x)cot(x))=2x+6csc(x)cot(x), matching option c.

after.name: Question 2
after.worked_solution:
We take the derivative of each term and then add them, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({x}^{2}-6csc⁡x) \\  & =2x-6(-csc⁡xcot⁡x) \\  & =2x+6csc⁡xcot⁡x\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Question 3
?
Find g′(π4) if g(x)=csc⁡x−2x3+cos⁡x.
g′(π4)=
Submit

decision.explanation: Differentiating gives g'(x)=-csc(x)cot(x)-6x^2-sin(x). At x=π/4, csc(x)=√2, cot(x)=1, and sin(x)=√2/2, so g'(π/4)=-3π^2/8-3√2/2.

after.name: Question 3
after.worked_solution:
We take the derivative of each term and then add them, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{g}^{′}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(-csc⁡x-2{x}^{3}+cos⁡x) \\  & =(-csc⁡xcot⁡x)-2\cdot 3{x}^{2}+(-sin⁡x) \\  & =-csc⁡xcot⁡x-6{x}^{2}-sin⁡x\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we substitute $x=\frac{\pi }{4}$ in the derivative and get

$$
\begin{aligned}{g}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{4}) & =-csc\,(\frac{\pi }{4})cot\,(\frac{\pi }{4})-6{(\frac{\pi }{4})}^{2}-sin\,(\frac{\pi }{4}) \\  & =-\sqrt{2}\cdot 1-6\cdot \frac{{\pi }^{2}}{16}-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2} \\  & =-\sqrt{2}-\frac{3}{8}{\pi }^{2}-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2} \\  & =-\frac{3\sqrt{2}}{2}-\frac{3}{8}{\pi }^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

g′(π4)=
−3π28​−3√22​
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

We take the derivative of each term and then add them, as follows:

g′(x)=ddx(−csc⁡x−2x3+cos⁡x)=(−csc⁡xcot⁡x)−2⋅3x2+(−sin⁡x)=−csc⁡xcot⁡x−6x2−sin⁡x

Then, we substitute x=π4 in the derivative and get

g′(π4)=−csc(π4)cot(π4)−6(π4)2−sin(π4)=−2⋅1−6⋅π216−22=−2−38π2−22=−322−38π2.

Question 4
?

Find f′(π2) if f(x)=ln⁡x−5csc⁡x.

a
2π+5
b
2π
c
10π
d
10
e
2π−5
Submit

decision.explanation: Differentiating gives f'(x)=1/x+5csc(x)cot(x). Since csc(π/2)=1 and cot(π/2)=0, f'(π/2)=2/π, matching option b.

after.name: Question 4
after.worked_solution:
We take the derivative of each term and then add them, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(ln⁡x-5csc⁡x) \\  & =\frac{1}{x}-5(-csc⁡xcot⁡x) \\  & =\frac{1}{x}+5csc⁡xcot⁡x\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we substitute $x=\frac{\pi }{2}$ in the derivative and get

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{2}) & =\frac{1}{(\frac{\pi }{2})}+5csc⁡(\frac{\pi }{2})cot⁡(\frac{\pi }{2}) \\  & =\frac{2}{\pi }+5\cdot 1\cdot 0 \\  & =\frac{2}{\pi }.\end{aligned}
$$

before.html:
Question 8
?

Find f′(x) if f(x)=5x−cot⁡x.

a
 5xln⁡5+csc⁡x
b
 5xln⁡5−csc2⁡x
c
 5xln⁡5+csc2⁡x
d
 5x−csc2⁡x
e
 5xln⁡5−csc⁡x
Submit

decision.explanation: The derivative of 5^x is 5^x ln(5), and the derivative of -cot(x) is +csc²(x). Therefore f'(x)=5^x ln(5)+csc²(x), matching option c.

after.name: Question 8
after.worked_solution:
We take the derivative of each term and then add them, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({5}^{x}-cot⁡x) \\  & ={5}^{x}ln⁡5-(-{csc}^{2}⁡x) \\  & ={5}^{x}ln⁡5+{csc}^{2}⁡x\end{aligned}
$$

Question 9
?

Find dydx if y=−2x4cot⁡x.

a
x4csc2⁡x+8x3cot⁡x
b
2x4csc2⁡x+8x3tan⁡x
c
2x4csc2⁡x−8x3cot⁡x
d
2x4cot2⁡x−8x3csc⁡x
e
2x2csc⁡x−8x3cot⁡x
Submit

decision.explanation: By the product rule, y'=(-8x^3)cot(x)+(-2x^4)(-csc²(x))=2x^4csc²(x)-8x^3cot(x), matching option c.

after.name: Question 9
after.worked_solution:
We calculate the derivative using the product rule, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(-2{x}^{4}cot⁡x) \\  & =(-8{x}^{3})(cot⁡x)+(-2{x}^{4})(-{csc}^{2}⁡x) \\  & =-8{x}^{3}cot⁡x+2{x}^{4}{csc}^{2}⁡x\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Question 9
?

Find dydx if y=−2x4cot⁡x.

a
x4csc2⁡x+8x3cot⁡x
b
2x4csc2⁡x+8x3tan⁡x
c
2x4csc2⁡x−8x3cot⁡x
d
2x4cot2⁡x−8x3csc⁡x
e
2x2csc⁡x−8x3cot⁡x
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

We calculate the derivative using the product rule, as follows:

dydx=ddx(−2x4cot⁡x)=(−8x3)(cot⁡x)+(−2x4)(−csc2⁡x)=−8x3cot⁡x+2x4csc2⁡x

verification.explanation: The worked solution confirms y'=(-8x^3)cot(x)+(-2x^4)(-csc²(x))=2x^4csc²(x)-8x^3cot(x), matching option c.

content.knowledge_point: Differentiating Expressions Involving the Cotangent Function
content.worked_solution:
We calculate the derivative using the product rule, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(-2{x}^{4}cot⁡x) \\  & =(-8{x}^{3})(cot⁡x)+(-2{x}^{4})(-{csc}^{2}⁡x) \\  & =-8{x}^{3}cot⁡x+2{x}^{4}{csc}^{2}⁡x\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Question 10

Find dydx if y=ln⁡(x)cot⁡(x).
dy
=
 cot⁡(x)+csc2⁡(x)⋅
dx xcot2⁡(x)
Submit

decision.explanation: The quotient rule gives y'=(cot(x)/x+ln(x)csc²(x))/cot²(x). Multiplying numerator and denominator by x gives (cot(x)+csc²(x)·x ln(x))/(x cot²(x)), so the blank is x ln(x).

after.name: Question 10
after.worked_solution:
We calculate the derivative using the quotient rule, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}\,(\frac{ln⁡(x)}{cot⁡(x)}) \\  & =\frac{cot⁡(x)\cdot \frac{1}{x}-ln⁡(x)(-{csc}^{2}⁡(x))}{{cot}^{2}⁡(x)} \\  & =\frac{(\frac{cot⁡(x)+xln⁡(x){csc}^{2}⁡(x)}{x})}{{cot}^{2}⁡(x)} \\  & =\frac{cot⁡(x)+{csc}^{2}⁡(x)\cdot xln⁡(x)}{x{cot}^{2}⁡(x)}\end{aligned}
$$

Question 11
?

Calculate dydx if y=3sin⁡x+sec⁡x.

a
−3cos⁡x−sec⁡xtan⁡x
b
3cos⁡x+sec⁡xtan⁡x
c
−3cos⁡x+sec⁡xtan⁡x
d
3cos⁡x−sec⁡xtan⁡x
e
3tan⁡x
Submit

decision.explanation: Differentiate each term: (3sin(x))'=3cos(x) and (sec(x))'=sec(x)tan(x). Thus y'=3cos(x)+sec(x)tan(x), matching option b.

after.name: Question 11
after.worked_solution:
We take the derivative of each term and then add them, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(3sin⁡x+sec⁡x) \\  & =3cos⁡x+sec⁡xtan⁡x\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Find the derivative of y=4sec⁡x+ex at x=0.
dydx|0=
Submit

decision.explanation: Differentiating gives y'=4sec(x)tan(x)+e^x. At x=0, sec(0)=1, tan(0)=0, and e^0=1, so y'(0)=1.

after.name: Question 12
after.worked_solution:
First, we take the derivative of each term and then add them:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}\,(4sec⁡x+{e}^{x}) \\  & =4sec⁡xtan⁡x+{e}^{x}\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we substitute $x=0$:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}{|}_{x=0} & =(4sec⁡xtan⁡x+{e}^{x})\,{|}_{x=0} \\  & =4sec⁡(0)tan⁡(0)+{e}^{0} \\  & =4\cdot 1\cdot 0+1 \\  & =1\end{aligned}
$$

before.html:
Question 13
?

Calculate dydx if y=3sec⁡xex.

a
3sec⁡x(tan⁡x−1)ex
b
3sec⁡x(tan⁡x−1)e2x
c
sec⁡x(3−tan⁡x)e2x
d
sec⁡x(3−tan⁡x)ex
e
sec⁡x(tan⁡x+1)3ex
Submit

decision.explanation: The quotient rule gives y'=(3sec(x)tan(x)e^x-3sec(x)e^x)/e^(2x)=3sec(x)(tan(x)-1)/e^x, matching option a.

after.name: Question 13
after.worked_solution:
We calculate the derivative using the quotient rule, as follows:

 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{3sec⁡x}{{e}^{x}}) \\  & =\frac{(3sec⁡xtan⁡x)({e}^{x})-(3sec⁡x)({e}^{x})}{({e}^{x})^{2}} \\  & =\frac{3{e}^{x}sec⁡x(tan⁡x-1)}{{e}^{2x}} \\  & =\frac{3sec⁡x(tan⁡x-1)}{{e}^{x}}\end{aligned}
$$

Question 13
?

Calculate dydx if y=3sec⁡xex.

a
3sec⁡x(tan⁡x−1)ex
b
3sec⁡x(tan⁡x−1)e2x
c
sec⁡x(3−tan⁡x)e2x
d
sec⁡x(3−tan⁡x)ex
e
sec⁡x(tan⁡x+1)3ex
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

We calculate the derivative using the quotient rule, as follows:

dydx=ddx(3sec⁡xex)=(3sec⁡xtan⁡x)(ex)−(3sec⁡x)(ex)(ex)2=3exsec⁡x(tan⁡x−1)e2x=3sec⁡x(tan⁡x−1)ex

content.knowledge_point: Differentiating Expressions Involving the Secant Function
content.worked_solution:
We calculate the derivative using the quotient rule, as follows:

 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{3sec⁡x}{{e}^{x}}) \\  & =\frac{(3sec⁡xtan⁡x)({e}^{x})-(3sec⁡x)({e}^{x})}{({e}^{x})^{2}} \\  & =\frac{3{e}^{x}sec⁡x(tan⁡x-1)}{{e}^{2x}} \\  & =\frac{3sec⁡x(tan⁡x-1)}{{e}^{x}}\end{aligned}
$$

decision.explanation: By the product rule, y'=5^x ln(5)sec(x)+5^x sec(x)tan(x)=5^x sec(x)(ln(5)+tan(x)), matching option d.

after.name: Question 14
after.worked_solution:
We calculate the derivative using the product rule, as follows:

 

$$

decision.explanation: The slope is f'(π/3). Since f'(x)=1/x-3csc(x)cot(x), csc(π/3)=2/√3, and cot(π/3)=1/√3, the slope is 3/π-3(2/3)=3/π-2, matching option e.

after.name: Question 16
after.problem: Find the slope of $y=f(x)$ at $x=\frac{\pi }{3}$ if $f(x)=ln⁡x+3csc⁡x.$
after.worked_solution:
First, we calculate the derivative using the sum rule:

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(ln⁡x+3csc⁡x) \\  & =\frac{1}{x}+3(-csc⁡xcot⁡x) \\  & =\frac{1}{x}-3csc⁡xcot⁡x\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we substitute $x=\frac{\pi }{3}$ in the derivative and get

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{3}) & =\frac{1}{(\frac{\pi }{3})}-3csc⁡(\frac{\pi }{3})cot⁡(\frac{\pi }{3}) \\  & =\frac{3}{\pi }-3(\frac{2}{\sqrt{3}})(\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}) \\  & =\frac{3}{\pi }-3(\frac{2}{3}) \\  & =\frac{3}{\pi }-2.\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

content.problem: Find the slope of $y=f(x)$ at $x=\frac{\pi }{3}$ if $f(x)=ln⁡x+3csc⁡x.$
content.worked_solution:
First, we calculate the derivative using the sum rule:

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(ln⁡x+3csc⁡x) \\  & =\frac{1}{x}+3(-csc⁡xcot⁡x) \\  & =\frac{1}{x}-3csc⁡xcot⁡x\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we substitute $x=\frac{\pi }{3}$ in the derivative and get

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{3}) & =\frac{1}{(\frac{\pi }{3})}-3csc⁡(\frac{\pi }{3})cot⁡(\frac{\pi }{3}) \\  & =\frac{3}{\pi }-3(\frac{2}{\sqrt{3}})(\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}) \\  & =\frac{3}{\pi }-3(\frac{2}{3}) \\  & =\frac{3}{\pi }-2.\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

decision.explanation: Differentiating gives f'(x)=-2x-5csc(x)cot(x). At x=π/6, csc(x)=2 and cot(x)=√3, so the slope is -π/3-10√3, matching option d.

after.name: Question 18
after.problem: Find the slope of $y=f(x)$ at $x=\frac{\pi }{6}$ if $f(x)=-{x}^{2}+5csc⁡x.$
after.worked_solution:
First, we calculate the derivative using the sum rule:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{d}{dx}(-{x}^{2}+5csc⁡x) \\  & =2\cdot (-x)+5(-csc⁡xcot⁡x) \\  & =-2x-5csc⁡xcot⁡x\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we substitute $x=\frac{\pi }{6}$ into the derivative and get:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{6}) & =-2(\frac{\pi }{6})-5csc⁡(\frac{\pi }{6})cot⁡(\frac{\pi }{6}) \\  & =-\frac{\pi }{3}-5\cdot 2\cdot \sqrt{3} \\  & =-\frac{\pi }{3}-10\sqrt{3}\end{aligned}
$$

decision.explanation: Differentiating gives f'(x)=sec(x)tan(x)/√3+6x/π. At x=π/3, sec(x)=2 and tan(x)=√3, so the slope is 2+2=4, matching option d.

after.name: Question 19
after.problem: Find the slope of $y=f(x)$ at $x=\frac{\pi }{3}$ if $f(x)=\frac{sec⁡x}{\sqrt{3}}+\frac{3{x}^{2}}{\pi }.$
after.worked_solution:
First, we take the derivative of each term and then add them, as follows:

 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{sec⁡x}{\sqrt{3}}+\frac{3{x}^{2}}{\pi }) \\  & =\frac{sec⁡xtan⁡x}{\sqrt{3}}+\frac{6x}{\pi }\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we substitute $x=\frac{\pi }{3}$ in the derivative and get

 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}{|}_{\pi /3} & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\cdot sec⁡(\frac{\pi }{3})\cdot tan⁡(\frac{\pi }{3})+\frac{6}{\pi }\cdot \frac{\pi }{3} \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\cdot 2\cdot \sqrt{3}+2 \\  & =2+2 \\  & =4.\end{aligned}
$$

EXPLANATION

First, we take the derivative of each term and then add them, as follows:

dydx=ddx(sec⁡x3+3x2π)=sec⁡xtan⁡x3+6xπ

Then, we substitute x=π3 in the derivative and get

dydx|π/3=13⋅sec⁡(π3)⋅tan⁡(π3)+6π⋅π3=13⋅2⋅3+2=2+2=4.

Question 20

Find the slope of y=f(x) at x=0 if f(x)=4xsec⁡x.
m=
Submit

decision.explanation: Since f(x)=4x cos(x), f'(x)=4cos(x)-4x sin(x). At x=0, the slope is 4·1-0=4.

after.name: Question 20
after.worked_solution:
First, we calculate the derivative using the quotient rule:

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{4x}{sec⁡x}) \\  & =\frac{\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(4x)\cdot sec⁡x-4x\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(sec⁡x)}{{sec}^{2}⁡x} \\  & =\frac{4sec⁡x-4x\cdot sec⁡xtan⁡x}{{sec}^{2}⁡x} \\  & =\frac{4sec⁡x(1-xtan⁡x)}{{sec}^{2}⁡x} \\  & =\frac{4(1-xtan⁡x)}{sec⁡x}\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we substitute $x=0$ in the derivative and get

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(0) & =\frac{4(1-0\cdot tan⁡0)}{sec⁡0} \\  & =\frac{4(1-0)}{1} \\  & =4\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$
